claims.text: The earlier provision in NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 dated 31st August 2023 established a per transaction limit of ₹500 and a maximum balance in the UPI LITE account of ₹2,000 with no change to the total limit.

The Addendum (2025-OC-169A) introduces new conditions allowing replenishment of used limits only in online mode with AFA and offering an option for Auto Top-up, whereas the earlier circular did not specify these replenishment mechanisms.

The Addendum (2025-OC-169A) includes a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant UPI LITE accounts with zero transactions in the past six months and refund balances to the source bank account, with implementation by 30th June 2025.

The earlier circular (2023-UPI-169) requested member banks and other payment providers to undertake requisite changes on App & application systems with immediate effect but did not specify a deadline for implementation of the limit enhancement.

The Addendum in Circular 169A revised UPI LITE limits from ₹500 per transaction to ₹1,000 and increased the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000, effective immediately as per its December 4, 2024 issuance, while also introducing a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant accounts with zero transactions in six months and refund their balances by June 30, 2025. The scope of the dormancy requirement applies only to accounts identified after the implementation deadline of June 30, 2025, as the circular does not specify retroactive application for pre-deadline dormant accounts.
claims.original_text: The Addendum in Circular 169A revised UPI LITE limits from ₹500 per transaction to ₹1,000 and increased the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000, effective immediately as per its December 4, 2024 issuance (S5), while also introducing a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant accounts with zero transactions in six months and refund their balances by June 30, 2025 (S7). The scope of the dormancy requirement applies only to accounts identified after the implementation deadline of June 30, 2025, as the circular does not specify retroactive application for pre-deadline dormant accounts (S7).

quotes.quote: NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 31st August 2023 To All Member-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam/Sir, **Subject: Enhancement in UPI LITE transaction limit to ₹500** UPI LITE has been designed to play a vital role in reducing infrastructure load on the Core Banking System of the banks. This feature has been making the small value transactions faster and highly reliable for transaction value below ₹200. As per the latest circular issued by RBI on 24th August, 2023 vide Circular No: RBI/2023-24/57 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S526/02-14-003/2023-24 with subject ‘Enhancing transaction limits for Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, the upper limit of an offline payment transaction is now increased from ₹200 to ₹500. In view of the above, the per transaction value limit for UPI LITE (Purpose code 44 - Online and 45 - Offline) has now been enhanced to ₹500. The details are as below: | UPI LITE Limit | Previous Limit | New Limit | |---|---|---| | Per Transaction | ₹200 | ₹500 | | Max balance in UPI lite account | ₹2000 | ₹2000 (No change) | The existing UPI pricing shall be applicable for transaction amount ₹201-₹500 for both P2P and P2M transactions. With reference to the above, Member Banks (Payee PSP), Third Party App providers (TPAPs), Merchants and other payment providers are requested to take note of the above enhancement

claims.text: The earlier provision in NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 dated 31st August 2023 established a per transaction limit of ₹500 and a maximum balance in the UPI LITE account of ₹2,000 with no change to the total limit.

The Addendum (2025-OC-169A) introduces new conditions allowing replenishment of used limits only in online mode with AFA and offering an option for Auto Top-up, whereas the earlier circular did not specify these replenishment mechanisms.

The Addendum (2025-OC-169A) includes a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant UPI LITE accounts with zero transactions in the past six months and refund balances to the source bank account, with implementation by 30th June 2025.

The earlier circular (2023-UPI-169) requested member banks and other payment providers to undertake requisite changes on App & application systems with immediate effect but did not specify a deadline for implementation of the limit enhancement.

The Addendum in Circular 169A revised UPI LITE limits from ₹500 per transaction to ₹1,000 and increased the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000, effective immediately as per its December 4, 2024 issuance, while also introducing a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant accounts with zero transactions in six months and refund their balances by June 30, 2025. The scope of the dormancy requirement applies only to accounts identified after the implementation deadline of June 30, 2025, as the circular does not specify retroactive application for pre-deadline dormant accounts.
claims.original_text: The Addendum in Circular 169A revised UPI LITE limits from ₹500 per transaction to ₹1,000 and increased the total account limit from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000, effective immediately as per its December 4, 2024 issuance (S5), while also introducing a new requirement for issuer banks to identify dormant accounts with zero transactions in six months and refund their balances by June 30, 2025 (S7). The scope of the dormancy requirement applies only to accounts identified after the implementation deadline of June 30, 2025, as the circular does not specify retroactive application for pre-deadline dormant accounts (S7).
